relativity.title: Special relativity — intro
relativity.body: Special relativity describes measurements in inertial frames. Its postulates are that physical laws have the same form in every inertial frame and light in vacuum has the same speed c for all inertial observers. Relative motion changes measured time intervals and lengths; rest energy is E₀ = mc².

contrast.en: Rest energy is not the whole energy of a moving particle.
contrast.ru: Энергия покоя не равна полной энергии движущейся частицы.

model.en: Length contraction concerns the direction of relative motion and simultaneous endpoint measurements in the observer’s frame.
model.ru: Сокращение длины относится к направлению движения и одновременным измерениям концов в системе наблюдателя.

quantum.title: Quantum mechanics — intro
quantum.body: Quantum mechanics uses states and probabilities to describe microscopic systems. Bound systems can have discrete allowed energies. Light exchanges energy in photons, each with E = hf. Quantum objects can show interference and localised detection events.

contrast.en: Quantisation does not mean that every physical quantity always has only discrete values.
contrast.ru: Квантование не означает, что любая физическая величина всегда принимает только дискретные значения.

model.en: Position and momentum distributions obey an uncertainty relation; this is not merely a limitation of imperfect instruments.
model.ru: Распределения координаты и импульса связаны соотношением неопределённостей; это не просто недостаток измерительных приборов.

thermo.title: Thermodynamics — laws
items: If A and B are each in thermal equilibrium with C, A and B are in thermal equilibrium with each other. Thermal equilibrium means no net heat transfer when they can exchange heat. This supports a common temperature scale.
The first law accounts for energy conservation: ΔU = Q − W, with Q positive for heat supplied to the system and W positive for work done by the system. U is internal energy.

The total entropy of an isolated system cannot decrease. It remains constant in an ideal reversible process and increases in an irreversible one. Entropy measures the distribution of energy among accessible microscopic states; “disorder” is only a loose analogy.
For a perfect crystal with a unique ground state, entropy tends to zero as absolute temperature tends to 0 K. Absolute zero cannot be reached by a finite thermodynamic cooling process.

zeroth.name: Zeroth law of thermodynamics
zeroth.rule: If A and B are each in thermal equilibrium with C, A and B are in thermal equilibrium with each other. Thermal equilibrium means no net heat transfer when they can exchange heat. This supports a common temperature scale.
examples: If a thermometer equilibrates at the same reading with two baths, the baths have the same temperature.

contrast.en: Equal temperatures do not imply equal internal energies.
contrast.ru: Одинаковые температуры не означают одинаковые внутренние энергии.

model.en: Objects must be allowed to reach thermal equilibrium before a thermometer reading represents their temperature.
model.ru: Показание термометра соответствует температуре тела после установления теплового равновесия.

first.name: First law (conservation of energy)
first.rule: The first law accounts for energy conservation: ΔU = Q − W, with Q positive for heat supplied to the system and W positive for work done by the system. U is internal energy.
examples: Supply 100 J of heat while the system does 30 J of work: ΔU = 70 J.

contrast.en: Heat and work are transfer processes; internal energy is a state quantity.
contrast.ru: Теплота и работа характеризуют передачу энергии; внутренняя энергия — состояние.

model.en: Other textbooks may define work done on the system as positive and write ΔU = Q + Won. State your convention.
model.ru: Другие учебники считают положительной работу над системой и пишут ΔU = Q + Wнад. Укажи соглашение о знаках.

second.name: Second law — entropy increases
second.rule: The total entropy of an isolated system cannot decrease. It remains constant in an ideal reversible process and increases in an irreversible one. Entropy measures the distribution of energy among accessible microscopic states; “disorder” is only a loose analogy.
examples: Heat spontaneously passes from hot water to cooler air, increasing total entropy.

contrast.en: Energy is conserved even when less of it can be converted into useful work.
contrast.ru: Энергия сохраняется, даже когда меньшую её часть можно превратить в полезную работу.

model.en: The restriction applies to the isolated whole; a refrigerator can lower entropy inside while increasing entropy more in its surroundings.
model.ru: Ограничение относится к изолированному целому; холодильник может уменьшать энтропию внутри, сильнее увеличивая её в окружении.

third.name: Third law — absolute zero
third.rule: For a perfect crystal with a unique ground state, entropy tends to zero as absolute temperature tends to 0 K. Absolute zero cannot be reached by a finite thermodynamic cooling process.
examples: 0 K corresponds to −273.15 °C; kelvin temperatures use no degree sign.

contrast.en: Zero temperature does not mean all quantum motion or energy disappears.
contrast.ru: Нулевая температура не означает исчезновения всех квантовых движений или энергии.

model.en: The zero-entropy statement needs the perfect-crystal and unique-ground-state conditions.
model.ru: Утверждение о нулевой энтропии требует идеального кристалла и единственного основного состояния.

astro.title: Astrophysics — basics
astro.body: Stars form when gas contracts under gravity. Main-sequence stars release energy by nuclear fusion in their cores. Later evolution depends on mass and composition; possible remnants include white dwarfs, neutron stars and black holes. The expanding-universe model is supported by galaxy redshifts and the cosmic microwave background.

contrast.en: Nuclear fusion combines nuclei; ordinary burning is a chemical rearrangement of electrons and bonds.
contrast.ru: При ядерном синтезе объединяются ядра; обычное горение — химическое изменение электронов и связей.

model.en: This is a broad evolutionary outline, not a rule that mass alone fixes every star’s outcome.
model.ru: Это общая схема эволюции, а не утверждение, что исход для любой звезды определяется только массой.

renewable.title: Renewable energy — engineering
renewable.body: Renewable energy resources are replenished on human timescales. Solar cells convert some incident radiation to electrical energy; wind and water turbines transfer energy from moving fluids; geothermal systems use energy from Earth’s interior.

contrast.en: Renewable describes replenishment, not unlimited output or zero environmental impact.
contrast.ru: Возобновляемость означает восполнение ресурса, а не неограниченную мощность или отсутствие воздействия на природу.

model.en: Available wind power scales as speed cubed for fixed swept area and air density; real electrical output also depends on efficiency and operating limits.
model.ru: Доступная мощность ветра пропорциональна кубу скорости при постоянных площади и плотности воздуха; реальная электрическая мощность зависит также от КПД и режима работы.

forceMotion.title: Force and Motion
forceMotion.intro: We study how and why objects move, what makes them speed up or stop, and what happens when they collide.

scalarsVectors.name: Scalars vs Vectors
scalarsVectors.rule: A scalar has a value without spatial direction. A vector has magnitude and direction and follows vector addition. Distance travelled is path length; displacement is the vector from start to finish.
examples: A 3 m eastward walk followed by 4 m north gives distance 7 m and displacement magnitude 5 m, about 53° north of east.
5 N right plus 3 N left gives 2 N right.

contrast.en: Distance travelled measures the entire path; displacement depends only on the two positions.
contrast.ru: Путь — длина всей траектории; перемещение зависит только от начального и конечного положений.

model.en: Choose a reference frame. A round trip has zero displacement even though its distance is nonzero.
model.ru: Укажи систему отсчёта. При возвращении в исходную точку перемещение равно нулю, хотя путь ненулевой.

newtonLaws.name: Newton's Three Laws
newtonLaws.rule: In an inertial frame: (1) zero resultant force means constant velocity; (2) for constant mass, ΣF = ma; (3) interacting bodies exert simultaneous equal and opposite forces on each other.
examples: A 30 N resultant on 10 kg gives 3 m/s².
The force of a table on a book and the force of the book on the table form a third-law pair; gravity and the table force on the book do not.

contrast.en: F is the resultant, not necessarily a single applied force.
contrast.ru: F — равнодействующая, которая может отличаться от отдельной приложенной силы.

model.en: The school equation assumes constant mass and speeds much smaller than light speed.
model.ru: Школьная формула предполагает постоянную массу и скорости намного меньше скорости света.

momentumImpulse.name: Momentum & Impulse
momentumImpulse.rule: Momentum p = mv is a vector. Net impulse J = FavgΔt equals Δp. A system’s total momentum is conserved over an interval if the net external impulse is zero.
examples: Stopping a 2 kg object moving at 3 m/s east requires impulse 6 N·s west.
For the same momentum change, a longer stopping time gives a smaller average force.

contrast.en: Momentum describes a state of motion; impulse describes its change.
contrast.ru: Импульс тела характеризует движение, а импульс силы — изменение импульса тела.

model.en: If force varies, use the average force or the signed area of a force–time graph.
model.ru: При переменной силе используй среднюю силу или площадь графика силы от времени с учётом знака.

motionGraphs.name: Motion graphs (interpretation)
motionGraphs.rule: The gradient of a distance–time graph gives speed; the gradient of a position–time graph gives velocity. A velocity–time gradient gives acceleration, and its signed area gives displacement. Total distance is the area under speed = |velocity|.
examples: At +3 m/s for 2 s and −3 m/s for 2 s, displacement is 0 m but distance is 12 m.
A negative gradient with negative velocity means increasing speed, not slowing.

contrast.en: An object can accelerate by changing direction while its speed stays constant.
contrast.ru: Ускорение возникает и при изменении направления движения с постоянным модулем скорости.

model.en: Negative acceleration means the negative axis direction; it means slowing only when opposite to velocity.
model.ru: Отрицательная проекция ускорения задаёт направление оси; торможение происходит, когда ускорение направлено против скорости.

terminalVelocity.name: Terminal velocity
terminalVelocity.rule: During falling in a fluid, drag usually grows with speed. A constant terminal velocity is reached when the upward fluid forces balance gravity, giving zero resultant and acceleration.
examples: Opening a parachute increases drag at the existing speed; the falling person slows until forces balance at a lower speed.
In a vacuum there is no drag-limited terminal velocity; acceleration still depends on the gravitational field.

contrast.en: Zero acceleration does not mean the object has stopped.
contrast.ru: Нулевое ускорение не означает остановку.

model.en: The terminal value depends on the fluid, shape and orientation; there is no drag-limited terminal speed in vacuum.
model.ru: Значение зависит от среды, формы и положения тела; в вакууме предельной скорости из-за сопротивления нет.

stoppingDistance.name: Stopping distance — thinking + braking
stoppingDistance.rule: Stopping distance = thinking distance + braking distance. At constant speed during reaction, thinking distance = vtreaction. With constant braking deceleration magnitude a, braking distance = v²/(2a).
examples: At 10 m/s, reaction time 1 s and braking deceleration 5 m/s² give 10 + 10 = 20 m.
At 20 m/s with the same reaction time and deceleration, the distances become 20 + 40 = 60 m.

contrast.en: Stopping distance also includes the distance travelled during the driver’s reaction.
contrast.ru: Остановочный путь включает также путь за время реакции водителя.

model.en: Distance is proportional to speed squared only if the braking deceleration remains the same.
model.ru: Зависимость от квадрата начальной скорости верна при одинаковом постоянном замедлении.

scalar.name: Scalar
scalar.definition: A physical quantity described by a numerical value and unit, with no spatial direction.
scalar.example: A mass of 2 kg is a scalar.

contrast.en: A vector also needs direction; a negative scalar need not describe a direction.
contrast.ru: Для вектора нужно направление; знак минус у скаляра не обязательно задаёт направление.

model.en: For example, −5 °C is a temperature, not a vector pointing backwards.
model.ru: Например, −5 °C — температура, а не вектор, направленный назад.

vector.name: Vector
vector.definition: A quantity with magnitude and direction that combines by vector addition.
vector.example: Forces of 5 N east and 3 N west give 2 N east.

contrast.en: Its magnitude is a scalar; the whole vector includes direction.
contrast.ru: Модуль — скаляр; сам вектор включает направление.

model.en: In one dimension, a signed component specifies direction relative to the chosen axis.
model.ru: При движении по прямой знак проекции указывает направление относительно выбранной оси.

displacement.name: Displacement
displacement.definition: The vector from an object’s initial position to its final position: Δr = rfinal − rinitial.
displacement.example: Walk 3 m east and then 1 m west: displacement is 2 m east; distance travelled is 4 m.

contrast.en: Distance travelled measures the entire path; displacement depends only on the two positions.
contrast.ru: Путь — длина всей траектории; перемещение зависит только от начального и конечного положений.

model.en: Choose a reference frame. A round trip has zero displacement even though its distance is nonzero.
model.ru: Укажи систему отсчёта. При возвращении в исходную точку перемещение равно нулю, хотя путь ненулевой.

velocity.name: Velocity
velocity.definition: The vector rate of change of position. Average velocity is displacement divided by elapsed time: vavg = Δr/Δt.
velocity.example: A 2 m eastward displacement in 4 s gives an average velocity of 0.5 m/s east.

contrast.en: Average speed uses total distance/time; instantaneous speed is the magnitude of instantaneous velocity.
contrast.ru: Средняя путевая скорость равна пути, делённому на время; мгновенная путевая скорость равна модулю вектора скорости.

model.en: Instantaneous velocity describes one moment; Δr/Δt over a finite interval gives an average.
model.ru: Мгновенная скорость относится к одному моменту; отношение Δr/Δt за конечный интервал даёт среднюю скорость.

acceleration.name: Acceleration
acceleration.definition: The vector rate of change of velocity; average acceleration is Δv/Δt, in m/s².
acceleration.example: Changing from 2 to 8 m/s east in 3 s gives 2 m/s² east.

contrast.en: An object can accelerate by changing direction while its speed stays constant.
contrast.ru: Ускорение возникает и при изменении направления движения с постоянным модулем скорости.

model.en: Negative acceleration means the negative axis direction; it means slowing only when opposite to velocity.
model.ru: Отрицательная проекция ускорения задаёт направление оси; торможение происходит, когда ускорение направлено против скорости.

resultantForce.name: Resultant force
resultantForce.definition: The vector sum of all forces acting on the chosen object.
resultantForce.example: 10 N right and 4 N left give a resultant of 6 N right.

contrast.en: Sum forces on one object; a third-law pair acts on different objects.
contrast.ru: Складывай силы на одном теле; силы пары третьего закона приложены к разным телам.

model.en: A zero resultant means zero acceleration, not necessarily zero velocity.
model.ru: Нулевая равнодействующая означает нулевое ускорение, но не обязательно нулевую скорость.

newton1.name: Newton's First Law
newton1.definition: In an inertial reference frame, an object with zero resultant force remains at rest or moves with constant velocity.
newton1.example: A puck continues straight at steady speed if horizontal forces are negligible.

contrast.en: Constant speed around a curve is not constant velocity.
contrast.ru: Постоянный модуль скорости на повороте не означает постоянного вектора скорости.

model.en: An inertial frame does not accelerate or rotate relative to another inertial frame.
model.ru: Инерциальная система не ускоряется и не вращается относительно другой инерциальной системы.

newton2.name: Newton's Second Law
newton2.definition: For constant mass in an inertial frame, resultant force equals mass times acceleration: ΣF = ma.
newton2.example: A 6 N resultant on 2 kg gives 3 m/s² in the force direction.

contrast.en: F is the resultant, not necessarily a single applied force.
contrast.ru: F — равнодействующая, которая может отличаться от отдельной приложенной силы.

model.en: The school equation assumes constant mass and speeds much smaller than light speed.
model.ru: Школьная формула предполагает постоянную массу и скорости намного меньше скорости света.

newton3.name: Newton's Third Law
newton3.definition: If A exerts a force on B, B simultaneously exerts an equal-magnitude, opposite-direction force on A.
newton3.example: A foot pushes the ground backwards; the ground pushes the foot forwards.

contrast.en: The two forces act on different bodies, so they do not balance on one body.
contrast.ru: Эти силы приложены к разным телам и не уравновешивают друг друга на одном теле.

model.en: Equal forces can cause unequal accelerations when the masses differ.
model.ru: Равные силы могут сообщать разные ускорения телам разной массы.

momentum.name: Momentum
momentum.definition: Linear momentum is mass multiplied by velocity, so it is a vector: p = mv, in kg·m/s.
momentum.example: A 2 kg trolley at 3 m/s east has momentum 6 kg·m/s east.

contrast.en: Momentum is a vector; kinetic energy is a scalar, ½mv².
contrast.ru: Импульс — вектор, а кинетическая энергия ½mv² — скаляр.

model.en: Use p = mv for nonrelativistic motion. Total momentum is conserved when external impulse is zero.
model.ru: Формула p = mv применяется при нерелятивистском движении. Суммарный импульс сохраняется при нулевом внешнем импульсе силы.

impulse.name: Impulse
impulse.definition: Impulse is the accumulated action of a force over time; net impulse equals the change in momentum.
impulse.example: For a constant or average resultant, J = FavgΔt = Δp, in N·s.

contrast.en: Momentum describes a state of motion; impulse describes its change.
contrast.ru: Импульс тела характеризует движение, а импульс силы — изменение импульса тела.

model.en: If force varies, use the average force or the signed area of a force–time graph.
model.ru: При переменной силе используй среднюю силу или площадь графика силы от времени с учётом знака.

terminalVelocity.name: Terminal velocity
terminalVelocity.definition: The constant falling velocity reached when drag and buoyancy together balance gravitational force.
terminalVelocity.example: For a skydiver, buoyancy is usually neglected, so drag ≈ mg at terminal velocity.

contrast.en: Zero acceleration does not mean the object has stopped.
contrast.ru: Нулевое ускорение не означает остановку.

model.en: The terminal value depends on the fluid, shape and orientation; there is no drag-limited terminal speed in vacuum.
model.ru: Значение зависит от среды, формы и положения тела; в вакууме предельной скорости из-за сопротивления нет.

reactionTime.name: Reaction time
reactionTime.definition: The interval between detecting a stimulus and beginning the response.
reactionTime.example: At 15 m/s, a 0.8 s reaction time gives 12 m thinking distance.

contrast.en: Reaction time is a duration; thinking distance is the distance travelled during it.
contrast.ru: Время реакции — длительность; путь за время реакции — расстояние.

model.en: Thinking distance = speed × reaction time assumes speed stays constant before braking.
model.ru: Формула пути за время реакции предполагает постоянную скорость до начала торможения.

brakingDistance.name: Braking distance
brakingDistance.definition: The distance travelled from when braking begins until the vehicle stops.
brakingDistance.example: At 10 m/s with constant deceleration 5 m/s², braking distance is 10 m.

contrast.en: Stopping distance also includes the distance travelled during the driver’s reaction.
contrast.ru: Остановочный путь включает также путь за время реакции водителя.

model.en: Distance is proportional to speed squared only if the braking deceleration remains the same.
model.ru: Зависимость от квадрата начальной скорости верна при одинаковом постоянном замедлении.

mass.name: Mass
mass.definition: A measure of an object’s inertia: for a given resultant force, greater mass gives less acceleration. SI unit: kilogram.
mass.example: A 2 kg object under 6 N has acceleration 3 m/s².

contrast.en: Mass is not a force; gravitational weight is mg and is measured in newtons.
contrast.ru: Масса — не сила; сила тяжести mg измеряется в ньютонах.

model.en: This inertial definition and F = ma use the constant-mass, nonrelativistic model.
model.ru: Это определение и F = ma используются в нерелятивистской модели с постоянной массой.

weight.name: Weight (gravitational force)
weight.definition: In this English course, weight is the gravitational force on an object: W = mg near Earth’s surface.
weight.example: A freely falling object still has gravitational weight even when a scale carried with it reads zero.

contrast.en: Russian school «вес» usually means the force a body exerts on a support or suspension; this differs from gravitational force.
contrast.ru: В русской школьной терминологии «вес» — сила действия тела на опору или подвес; это не то же самое, что сила тяжести.

model.en: For a stationary supported body their magnitudes may both equal mg, but the forces act on different objects.
model.ru: Для неподвижного тела модули могут быть равны mg, но силы приложены к разным телам.

forcesEnergy.title: Forces and Energy
forcesEnergy.intro: This page covers how forces stretch springs and do work. It also explains how energy is stored and transferred, and how pressure and density are defined and calculated.

hookesLaw.name: Hooke's Law — springs & elasticity
hookesLaw.rule: For an ideal linear spring F = kx, where x is extension from natural length and k is stiffness in N/m. This proportionality ends at the limit of proportionality. The elastic limit concerns whether deformation remains after unloading.
examples: A 200 N/m spring extends 0.03 m under 6 N within its linear range.
A rubber band stretches along a curved force–extension graph, yet it returns to its original length once the force is removed, provided it is not overstretched.

contrast.en: x is the extension, not the total length of the spring. If the natural length is L₀ and the spring stretches by x, its total length is L₀ + x.
contrast.ru: x — это удлинение, а не полная длина пружины. Если недеформированная длина равна L₀, а удлинение — x, то полная длина равна L₀ + x.

model.en: F = kx also works for compression: a compressed spring pushes back with force kx, as long as it stays within its limit of proportionality.
model.ru: Формула F = kx работает и при сжатии: сжатая пружина отталкивает с силой kx, пока сжатие не выходит за предел пропорциональности.

work.name: Work, energy & power
work.rule: Work transfers energy. For a constant force, W = Fd cos θ, where θ is the angle between the force and the displacement. Average power is the energy transferred per unit time: P = ΔE/Δt. Energy is measured in joules (J) and power in watts (W), where 1 W = 1 J/s.
examples: Transfer 60 J in 3 s: average power is 20 W.
A trolley rolls along a horizontal table. Its weight acts at 90° to the motion, so the weight does no work on it.

contrast.en: Force is measured in newtons (N), but work is measured in joules (J): one joule is the work done by a force of one newton acting through one metre. Writing newtons for work is a common mistake.
contrast.ru: Силу измеряют в ньютонах (Н), а работу — в джоулях (Дж): 1 Дж — работа силы 1 Н на пути 1 м, то есть 1 Дж = 1 Н·м. Записывать работу в ньютонах — частая ошибка.

model.en: W = Fd works only when the force points along the displacement. At an angle θ, use cos θ: a 10 N force at 60° to a 2 m displacement does 10 J of work, not 20 J.
model.ru: Формула A = F·s верна, только если сила направлена вдоль перемещения. При угле α в формулу входит cos α. Сила 10 Н под углом 60° к перемещению 2 м совершает работу 10 Дж, а не 20 Дж.

nonRenewableResources.name: Non-renewable energy resources
nonRenewableResources.rule: Non-renewable energy resources are energy sources that natural processes replace far too slowly to keep up with our use of them. Fossil fuels (coal, oil and natural gas) formed from the remains of ancient organisms over a very long time, so their supply is limited. Renewable resources, such as sunlight, wind and flowing water, are constantly renewed by natural processes.
examples: A coal mine supplies a power station. Each lump burned is used up for good, so the mine's supply only shrinks.
Uranium works the same way: the ore in the rock is finite and does not refill on a human timescale.

contrast.en: Non-renewable does not mean 'no longer used': most of our energy still comes from non-renewable fossil fuels.
contrast.ru: Невозобновляемый не значит «больше не используемый»: большая часть нашей энергии всё ещё приходится на невозобновляемое ископаемое топливо.

model.en: The key is the rate of replacement, not the timescale: can natural processes replace this source as fast as we use it? If not, it is non-renewable.
model.ru: Важна скорость восполнения, а не срок: успевают ли природные процессы восполнять этот источник так же быстро, как мы его используем? Если нет, ресурс невозобновляемый.

energyStores.name: Energy stores & transfers
energyStores.rule: Energy is a conserved quantity used to account for changes in a system. Examples of stores include kinetic, gravitational, elastic, internal and chemical energy. Work, heating and radiation describe ways energy is transferred.
examples: A dropped ball loses gravitational store as it falls and gains kinetic store. With no air resistance, the kinetic store gained equals the gravitational store lost.
A battery loses chemical store as it runs a fan, while the kinetic store of the blades and the internal store of the wires increase.

contrast.en: Energy is not used up. When brakes stop a car, its kinetic energy is transferred to the brakes and the road as internal energy.
contrast.ru: Энергия не «расходуется» и не исчезает. Когда тормоза останавливают машину, её кинетическая энергия превращается во внутреннюю энергию тормозов и дороги.

model.en: Store and transfer accounting counts how much energy there is, not how useful it is. Energy spread out as heat in a room still counts, but it is hard to use.
model.ru: Учёт запасов и передач энергии показывает, сколько энергии есть, но не насколько она полезна. Энергия, рассеянная в комнате в виде тепла, тоже учитывается, но её трудно использовать.

pressure.name: Pressure
pressure.rule: Average pressure is the normal force divided by the contact area: p = F/A, where F is the force perpendicular to the surface. In a fluid at rest, pressure at a point is the same in every direction, and each force acts at right angles to the surface it acts on.
examples: For 200 N over 0.04 m², p = 5000 Pa.
Snowshoes spread a person's weight over a larger area, so the pressure on the snow is lower and the person sinks less.

contrast.en: Use the contact area (the base), not the total surface area of the object. A 100 N box on a 0.5 m × 0.2 m base exerts 100 N ÷ 0.1 m² = 1000 Pa.
contrast.ru: В формулу подставляют площадь опоры (основание), а не площадь всей поверхности тела. Коробка весом 100 Н опирается основанием 0,5 м × 0,2 м и создаёт давление 100 Н ÷ 0,1 м² = 1000 Па.

model.en: The formula gives the average pressure over the contact area. If the load is uneven, some points feel more pressure than others, as under the point of a drawing pin.
model.ru: Формула даёт среднее давление по площади опоры. Если нагрузка неравномерна, в одних точках давление больше, чем в других, например под острием канцелярской кнопки.

density.name: Density & floating
density.rule: Density is mass per unit volume. The buoyant force equals the weight of the fluid the object displaces. A freely floating object has an average density less than the fluid's. If the densities are equal, the object stays in balance at any depth where it is placed.
examples: A hollow steel ship floats because its total mass divided by the whole volume enclosed by its hull (including the air inside) is below the density of water.
A solid block of density 3 g/cm³ sinks in water of density about 1 g/cm³.

contrast.en: A floating object is not held up by a force larger than its weight. At rest, the buoyant force equals the object's weight.
contrast.ru: Плавающее тело держится на воде силой, равной его силе тяжести, а не большей. Когда тело покоится, выталкивающая сила равна его силе тяжести.

model.en: The same test works for any fluid, including air: a helium balloon rises because its average density is lower than that of the surrounding air.
model.ru: Тот же критерий работает для любой жидкости и для газов, включая воздух: гелиевый шар поднимается, потому что его средняя плотность меньше плотности окружающего воздуха.

fluidPressure.name: Fluid pressure & atmospheric pressure
fluidPressure.rule: For a fluid at rest with constant density, the pressure at depth h is p = p₀ + Δp, where p₀ is the pressure at the surface and Δp = ρgh is the increase in pressure below the surface. Atmospheric pressure normally falls with altitude, because less air lies above each level.
examples: At 2 m in water with ρ = 1000 kg/m³ and g = 9.8 m/s², the pressure increase is 19 600 Pa.
At 2 m, with the water surface open to air (p₀ ≈ 1.01 × 10⁵ Pa), the absolute pressure is about 1.2 × 10⁵ Pa.

contrast.en: Depth is not the height above the bottom. Depth h runs from the liquid's surface down to the point, so a point near the base of a deep tank is at great depth, while a point near the top is shallow.
contrast.ru: Глубина — это не высота над дном. Глубина h отсчитывается от поверхности жидкости вниз до точки: точка у дна глубокого сосуда лежит на большой глубине, а точка у самой поверхности — на небольшой.

model.en: Water density is almost constant, so Δp = ρgh works well for depths of a few metres. Air density falls with height, so for the atmosphere over kilometres, Δp = ρgh gives only a rough estimate.
model.ru: Плотность воды почти постоянна, поэтому формула Δp = ρgh хорошо работает на глубинах в несколько метров. Плотность воздуха уменьшается с высотой, поэтому для атмосферы на высотах в несколько километров Δp = ρgh даёт лишь грубую оценку.

contactForce.name: Contact force
contactForce.definition: An interaction force acting through contact between objects.
contactForce.example: A table exerts a normal contact force on a book.

contrast.en: Gravity can act without contact; friction needs a contact interaction.
contrast.ru: Тяготение действует без соприкосновения; трение связано с контактом.

model.en: At the microscopic level, ordinary contact forces arise mainly from electromagnetic interactions.
model.ru: На микроскопическом уровне обычные контактные силы обусловлены главным образом электромагнитным взаимодействием.

sources.title: Morris, Physics for the IB MYP 4 & 5: By Concept (Hodder)

nonContactForce.name: Non-contact force
nonContactForce.definition: A force between objects that does not require them to touch.
nonContactForce.example: Earth pulls an orbiting satellite by gravity, even though the two never touch.

contrast.en: The pull of gravity on a book is a non-contact force; the table's upward push on the book is a contact force.
contrast.ru: Сила тяжести, действующая на книгу, — бесконтактная; сила, с которой стол поддерживает книгу, — контактная.

model.en: Fields describe the interaction; “non-contact” does not mean that no physical interaction occurs.
model.ru: Взаимодействие описывается полем; отсутствие контакта не означает отсутствия взаимодействия.

sources.title: Morris, Physics for the IB MYP 4 & 5: By Concept (Hodder)

elasticity.name: Elasticity
elasticity.definition: The property of recovering the original shape and size after a deforming force is removed.
elasticity.example: An elastic spring returns to its original length when unloaded.

contrast.en: Elastic deformation is reversible; plastic deformation leaves a permanent change.
contrast.ru: Упругая деформация обратима; пластическая оставляет остаточное изменение.

model.en: An elastic material need not obey a linear force–extension relation.
model.ru: Упругий материал не обязательно имеет линейную зависимость силы от удлинения.

sources.title: Morris, Physics for the IB MYP 4 & 5: By Concept (Hodder)

hookesLaw.name: Hooke's Law
hookesLaw.definition: Within the proportional range, the size of the applied force is proportional to a spring's extension: F = kx.
hookesLaw.example: For k = 100 N/m and x = 0.02 m, F = 2 N.

contrast.en: Hooke's law is a formula, not the force itself. The spring force can act beyond the limit of proportionality, where F = kx no longer describes it; the limit of proportionality is distinct from the elastic limit.
contrast.ru: Закон Гука — это формула, а не сама сила. Сила упругости может действовать и за пределом пропорциональности, где F = kx уже не описывает её; предел пропорциональности отличается от предела упругости.

model.en: Within the proportional range, k is numerically equal to the force needed to stretch the spring by 1 m. Its unit is N/m, and a stiffer spring has a larger k.
model.ru: В пределах пропорциональности коэффициент жёсткости k численно равен силе, которая растягивает пружину на 1 м. Единица k — Н/м. У более жёсткой пружины k больше.

sources.title: Morris, Physics for the IB MYP 4 & 5: By Concept (Hodder)

workDone.name: Work done
workDone.definition: Work done is the energy transferred when a force moves an object in the direction of the force.
workDone.example: A 10 N force along a 2 m displacement does 20 J of work.

contrast.en: A large force can do no work: holding a heavy bag still means exerting a force, but the bag has no displacement, so W = 0.
contrast.ru: Большая сила может не совершать работу: удерживая тяжёлую сумку неподвижно, мы прикладываем силу, но перемещения нет, поэтому A = 0.

model.en: Work done is negative when the force opposes the displacement (θ > 90°). The body then loses kinetic energy, as a box sliding under friction does.
model.ru: Работа отрицательна, если сила направлена против перемещения (α > 90°). Тогда тело теряет кинетическую энергию, как ящик, который скользит и тормозится силой трения.

energyTransfer.name: Energy transfer
energyTransfer.definition: Energy passing from one system to another by work, heating or radiation.
energyTransfer.example: An electric current does work in a heater, which then transfers energy to the water by heating.

contrast.en: A transfer moves energy between systems. A transformation changes energy from one form to another inside one system.
contrast.ru: Передача переносит энергию между системами. Превращение — переход энергии из одного вида в другой внутри одной системы.

model.en: Count a transfer only when energy crosses the boundary of the chosen system. Energy moving inside the system only redistributes between its stores.
model.ru: Считай передачей только переход энергии через границу выбранной системы. Внутри системы энергия лишь перераспределяется между её запасами.

pressure.name: Pressure
pressure.definition: Pressure is the force acting perpendicular to a surface, divided by the area of that surface: p = F/A, measured in pascals (Pa).
pressure.example: A force of 600 N acts on shoe soles with a total area of 0.03 m², so the pressure is 20 kPa.

contrast.en: The formula p = F/A applies to any surface, but Δp = ρgh is only the extra pressure that a column of liquid at rest adds.
contrast.ru: Формула p = F/S применима к любой поверхности, а Δp = ρgh — лишь прибавка давления, которую создаёт столб покоящейся жидкости.

model.en: One pascal is one newton per square metre: a force of 1 N spread over 1 m² gives 1 Pa.
model.ru: Один паскаль — это один ньютон на квадратный метр: сила 1 Н, распределённая по площади 1 м², создаёт давление 1 Па.

atmosphericPressure.name: Atmospheric pressure
atmosphericPressure.definition: Pressure exerted by the surrounding atmosphere on a surface.
atmosphericPressure.example: A standard atmosphere is 101 325 Pa; actual pressure changes with weather and altitude.

contrast.en: Atmospheric pressure acts in all directions, not only downwards.
contrast.ru: Атмосферное давление действует во всех направлениях, а не только вниз.

model.en: It acts on the outside of any surface exposed to air. Inside a sealed container, the gas itself sets the pressure, not the outside air.
model.ru: Атмосферное давление действует снаружи на любую поверхность, соприкасающуюся с воздухом. Внутри закрытого сосуда давление задаёт сам газ, а не наружный воздух.

density.name: Density
density.definition: Mass per unit volume: ρ = m/V, in kg/m³.
density.example: A mass of 200 g in 100 cm³ has density 2 g/cm³, which is 2000 kg/m³.

contrast.en: Density is not the same as mass: a large polystyrene block can have less mass than a small steel block.
contrast.ru: Плотность — не то же, что масса: большой блок пенопласта может иметь меньшую массу, чем маленький стальной.

model.en: One density value applies to a uniform material at a stated temperature. For a gas, pressure matters too, because its density changes a lot with both.
model.ru: Одно значение плотности относится к однородному веществу при заданной температуре. Для газа важно ещё и давление: его плотность сильно меняется и от температуры, и от давления.

fluidPressure.name: Fluid pressure
fluidPressure.definition: Pressure within a liquid or gas, producing normal forces on surfaces in contact with it.
fluidPressure.example: At 100 m depth in fresh water, the pressure increase from the water column alone is Δp = ρgh = 1000 kg/m³ × 9.8 m/s² × 100 m = 9.8 × 10⁵ Pa.

contrast.en: In a liquid, pressure depends on depth and density, not on the shape of the container or the amount of liquid.
contrast.ru: В жидкости давление зависит от глубины и плотности, но не от формы сосуда и количества жидкости.

model.en: The pressure on the surface (p₀) is atmospheric only if the vessel is open; in a sealed vessel, use the value given in the question.
model.ru: Давление на поверхности (p₀) равно атмосферному, только если сосуд открыт; в закрытом сосуде используй значение из условия.

energy.name: Energy
energy.definition: The capacity of a system to do work. Its SI unit is the joule (J).
energy.example: A moving object has kinetic energy; lifting an object increases gravitational potential energy of the object–Earth system.

contrast.en: Energy measures an amount; power measures the rate at which it is transferred.
contrast.ru: Энергия характеризует количество, мощность — скорость её передачи.

model.en: Specify the system boundary and reference level for potential energy.
model.ru: Укажи границы системы и нулевой уровень потенциальной энергии.

power.name: Power
power.definition: Power is the rate at which energy is transferred: P = E/t, measured in watts (W).
power.example: A 1500 W kettle running for 120 s transfers 180 kJ of energy.

contrast.en: A high-power device need not use more total energy if it runs for less time.
contrast.ru: Большая мощность не обязательно означает больший расход энергии, если прибор работает меньше времени.

model.en: For a time interval, the average power is used: energy = power × time holds only when the power is constant.
model.ru: За промежуток времени используют среднюю мощность. Формула A = Nt верна только при постоянной мощности.

sources.title: Morris, Physics for the IB MYP 4 & 5: By Concept (Hodder)
sources.section: p. 226–233 (Putting energy to work) — по выписке SOURCES, не пересверено (открыто)

heat.name: Heat
heat.definition: Energy transferred between systems because of a temperature difference; symbol Q, unit joule.
heat.example: A cup of tea at 90 °C in a room at 20 °C transfers heat to the air until their temperatures are equal.

contrast.en: Internal energy is stored in a body, but heat is only a transfer of energy, not a store.
contrast.ru: Внутренняя энергия (internal energy) хранится в теле, а теплота — это процесс передачи энергии, а не запас.

model.en: Heat supplied does not always raise temperature: while ice melts at 0 °C, the heat turns ice into water and the temperature stays at 0 °C.
model.ru: Подведённая теплота не всегда повышает температуру: пока лёд тает при 0 °C, теплота превращает его в воду, а температура остаётся равной 0 °C.

temperature.name: Temperature
temperature.definition: Temperature is a measure of how hot or cold a body is. Heat flows spontaneously from a higher temperature to a lower one.
temperature.example: A thermometer placed in water at 40 °C shows 40 °C once it has reached the water's temperature.

contrast.en: Temperature is not total internal energy: a large cool bath can have more internal energy than a small hot cup.
contrast.ru: Температура не равна полной внутренней энергии: большая прохладная ванна может иметь больше внутренней энергии, чем маленькая горячая чашка.

model.en: Temperature is a measure of the average kinetic energy of the particles: in a hotter substance, the particles move faster on average.
model.ru: Температура — мера средней кинетической энергии частиц вещества: в более горячем веществе частицы в среднем движутся быстрее.

sim1.title: Hooke's Law
sim1.desc: Change the spring constant and the force to see the extension of this ideal linear spring. The dashed line marks the limit of proportionality used in this model.
sim1.warning: Beyond the limit of proportionality: x = F/k is only an extrapolation, not a prediction for a real spring. It says nothing about permanent deformation.

sim2.title: Pressure (p = F / A)
sim2.desc: Vary the force and the contact area. The force is spread evenly over the contact area, so the result is the average pressure.

sim3.title: Density & Floating
sim3.desc: Compare average object density with fluid density. The model omits surface tension and external supports.

sim4.title: Fluid Pressure with Depth
sim4.desc: Set the depth and the liquid density; the liquid is at rest and has the same density everywhere. The value shown is Δp = ρgh, the pressure increase from the liquid column; add the surface pressure p₀ to get the absolute pressure.

simEnergy.title: Energy Transformations (Pendulum)
simEnergy.desc: Watch potential and kinetic energy change into each other as the pendulum swings.
simEnergy.modelCaption: This model ignores friction and air resistance, so an ideal pendulum keeps its mechanical energy constant. The simulation adds a small extra damping for stability, which makes the displayed mechanical energy decrease slowly.

simWorkPower.title: Work and Power
simWorkPower.desc: Change the mass, height and time, and check W = mgh and average power P = W / t. The load lifts at steady speed with no losses, so the lifting force equals mg.

electricity.title: Electricity and Magnetism
electricity.intro: Charge, current, voltage and resistance are the core ideas. The topic also covers circuits, power and energy, magnetism, and the sensors and safety devices used in circuits.

currentVoltageResistance.name: How current, voltage and resistance are linked
currentVoltageResistance.rule: Current I = ΔQ/Δt is the charge that passes a point per unit time. Potential difference V = E/Q is the energy transferred per coulomb of charge. Resistance R = V/I links the three quantities: if you know any two, you can find the third.
examples: 2 C in 1 s means 2 A. At 6 V, each coulomb transfers 6 J.
6 V across a component carrying 2 A gives 3 Ω.

contrast.en: Potential difference is not energy, but energy per coulomb. So the volt and the joule are different units.
contrast.ru: Напряжение — не энергия, а энергия на кулон заряда. Поэтому вольт и джоуль — разные единицы.

model.en: R = V/I applies to one component or section: measure V across it and I through it.
model.ru: Формула R = U/I относится к одному элементу или участку: U измеряют на нём, I — через него.

sources.title: Morris, Physics for the IB MYP 4 & 5: By Concept (Hodder, 2015)

ohmsLaw.name: Ohm's law (V = IR)
ohmsLaw.rule: For an ohmic conductor at fixed temperature and physical conditions, current is proportional to potential difference. Its I–V graph is a straight line through the origin, and R = V/I remains constant.
examples: Doubling voltage across a fixed 10 Ω resistor doubles current.
A filament lamp heats as current rises, so its resistance changes and the graph curves.

contrast.en: Any component has a V/I ratio, so writing R = V/I does not prove Ohm's law. The law needs R to stay constant.
contrast.ru: У любого элемента есть отношение U/I, поэтому одна лишь запись R = U/I не доказывает закон Ома. Закон выполняется только тогда, когда R остаётся постоянным.

model.en: A straight I–V graph confirms the law only over the range where R stays constant. Where the graph curves, the law does not apply.
model.ru: Прямая на графике I(U) подтверждает закон только в том диапазоне, где R остаётся постоянным. Там, где график изгибается, закон не выполняется.

sources.title: Morris, Physics for the IB MYP 4 & 5: By Concept (Hodder, 2015)

seriesParallel.name: How series and parallel circuits differ
seriesParallel.rule: In series, current is common, potential differences add and resistor values add. In parallel, potential difference is common, branch currents add and 1/Req = 1/R₁ + 1/R₂ + ….
examples: Two 4 Ω resistors give 8 Ω in series and 2 Ω in parallel.
An open branch interrupts that branch; an open unbranched series path interrupts the whole path.

contrast.en: An ammeter goes in series, so it carries the same current as the component. A voltmeter goes in parallel.
contrast.ru: Амперметр включают последовательно, поэтому через него идёт тот же ток, что и через элемент. Вольтметр включают параллельно.

model.en: The rules hold only if the connecting wires have negligible resistance.
model.ru: Правила верны, только если сопротивлением соединительных проводов можно пренебречь.

sources.title: Morris, Physics for the IB MYP 4 & 5: By Concept (Hodder, 2015)

power.name: Electrical power
power.rule: Electrical power is the energy transferred per second, measured in watts (W). For an electrical component, P = VI, where P is power in watts (W), V is potential difference in volts (V) and I is current in amperes (A). At constant power, the energy transferred is E = Pt, where E is energy in joules (J) and t is time in seconds (s). Using E = Pt, 1 kWh = 1000 W × 3600 s = 3.6 × 10⁶ J.
examples: A 60 W device running 2 h transfers 120 Wh = 0.12 kWh.
At 12 V and 2 A, power is 24 W.

contrast.en: P = VI holds for any electrical component. P = I²R and P = V²/R hold only for a resistor.
contrast.ru: P = UI верно для любого элемента цепи. Формулы P = I²R и P = U²/R верны только для резистора.

model.en: E = Pt holds only for constant power. For an appliance that switches on and off, use its average power or a measured total energy.
model.ru: A = Pt верно только при постоянной мощности. Для прибора, который периодически включается и выключается, используй среднюю мощность или измеренную суммарную энергию.

sources.title: Morris, Physics for the IB MYP 4 & 5: By Concept (Hodder, 2015)

safety.name: Mains electricity & safety
safety.rule: Excess current heats the wiring. Protection devices open the circuit: a fuse melts, and a circuit breaker switches off when the current is dangerously large. Earthing gives a fault current an alternative path, so the protection can act.
examples: A short circuit may produce excessive current and operate overcurrent protection.
If a live wire touches a metal casing, the fault current can flow through the earth connection, and the fuse or circuit breaker may switch the circuit off.

contrast.en: Earthing does not absorb the current, and it does not switch the circuit off by itself. A fuse or circuit breaker does that.
contrast.ru: Заземление не «поглощает» ток и само цепь не отключает. Это делает предохранитель или автоматический выключатель.

model.en: Earthing works only for equipment connected to earth, for example through an earth pin in the plug.
model.ru: Заземление работает только у оборудования, подключённого к земле, например через заземляющий контакт (earth pin) в вилке.

magnetism.name: Magnetism & electromagnetism
magnetism.rule: An electric current produces a magnetic field around it. Around a straight wire, the field lines form circles that surround the wire. Their direction follows the right-hand rule for conventional current, which flows from positive to negative.
examples: If the current in a straight wire is reversed, the field lines circle the wire in the opposite direction.
Inside a solenoid (a coil carrying current), the field is uniform, except near the ends of the coil.

contrast.en: Field lines show field direction; they are not physical wires or particle tracks.
contrast.ru: Линии поля показывают направление поля; это не провода и не траектории частиц.

circuitSymbols.name: Circuit symbols and reading a diagram
circuitSymbols.rule:
A circuit diagram shows a circuit with standard symbols, so anyone can build the same circuit from it. Read the diagram from the battery, following the wires.

- Cell: a long thin line (positive) and a short thick line (negative). A battery is two or more cells joined together.
- Switch: a gap in the wire. A closed switch connects the wire; an open switch keeps the gap.
- Lamp (bulb): a circle with a cross inside.
- Resistor: a rectangle.
- Ammeter: a circle with the letter A. It is connected in series, in a break in the wire.
- Voltmeter: a circle with the letter V. It is connected in parallel, across the component.

A dot where wires meet shows a junction. Wires that cross without a dot are not connected.
examples: A bulb in a circuit diagram is a circle with a cross inside, not a picture of a bulb.
To measure the current through a lamp, put the ammeter in series with the lamp. To measure the voltage across the lamp, put the voltmeter in parallel with the lamp.

contrast.en: The ammeter and the voltmeter are both circles; only the letter inside (A or V) tells them apart.
contrast.ru: Амперметр и вольтметр на схеме — оба кружки; различает их только буква внутри (A или V).

model.en: The symbols show connections, not the real size or shape of the parts. The long and short lines of a cell show polarity, not its size.
model.ru: Символы показывают соединения, а не реальные размеры и форму деталей. Длинная и короткая линии элемента показывают полярность, а не размер элемента.

current.name: Current
current.definition: The rate at which electric charge passes a cross-section: Iavg = ΔQ/Δt, in amperes.
current.example: 6 C passing in 3 s gives an average current of 2 A.

contrast.en: Current is not used up in a component: as much charge leaves it as enters it. Energy is transferred to the component instead.
contrast.ru: Ток в элементе не расходуется: сколько заряда входит в элемент, столько и выходит. Вместо этого элементу передаётся энергия.

model.en: The direction of current is a convention, from + to −. In metals the charge carriers are electrons, which move the other way.
model.ru: Направление тока условное: от «+» к «−». В металлах носители заряда — электроны, и они движутся в обратную сторону.

voltage.name: Voltage
voltage.definition: Voltage, also called potential difference (p.d.), is the energy transferred per coulomb of charge between two points: V = E/Q, measured in volts (V).
voltage.example: A 1.5 V cell gives 1.5 J of energy to every coulomb of charge that flows through it.

contrast.en: Voltage is measured across a component, but current is measured through it.
contrast.ru: Напряжение измеряют на элементе, а ток — через него.

model.en: The volt follows from the definition: 1 V = 1 J/C.
model.ru: Единица вольт следует из определения: 1 В = 1 Дж/Кл.

resistance.name: Resistance
resistance.definition: Resistance is the ratio of the potential difference across a component to the current through it: R = V/I, measured in ohms (Ω).
resistance.example: A resistor with 5 V across it and 0.25 A through it has resistance 20 Ω.

contrast.en: Resistance belongs to one component or section of a circuit; resistivity is a property of the material itself.
contrast.ru: Сопротивление относится к одному элементу цепи или её участку; удельное сопротивление (resistivity) — свойство самого материала.

model.en: One ohm is the resistance of a component that passes 1 A when 1 V is across it.
model.ru: Один ом — сопротивление элемента, через который при напряжении 1 В проходит ток 1 А.

sources.title: Morris, Physics for the IB MYP 4 & 5: By Concept (Hodder, 2015)

charge.name: Charge
charge.definition: Charge is a property of particles and objects that makes them take part in electric interactions. It is positive or negative and is measured in coulombs (C).
charge.example: One electron carries a charge of about −1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, so a charge of 1 C is carried by about 6.25 × 10¹⁸ electrons.

contrast.en: A neutral object can contain charged particles whose charges sum to zero.
contrast.ru: Нейтральное тело содержит заряженные частицы, суммарный заряд которых равен нулю.

model.en: Charge is conserved: when bodies become charged, electrons move from one to another and the total charge does not change.
model.ru: Заряд сохраняется: при электризации электроны переходят с одного тела на другое, а суммарный заряд не меняется.

seriesCircuit.name: Series circuit
seriesCircuit.definition: A series circuit has its components joined one after another along a single path, with no branches. Current is the same at every point of it, because there is only one path for the charge.
seriesCircuit.example: A 9 V supply connected to two 3 Ω resistors in series has a total resistance of 6 Ω and a current of 1.5 A. Each resistor has 4.5 V across it.

contrast.en: The same current does not mean the same voltage: at one current, the resistor with the larger resistance has the larger voltage across it.
contrast.ru: Одинаковый ток не означает одинакового напряжения: при одном токе на резисторе с большим сопротивлением напряжение больше.

model.en: The rule R = R₁ + R₂ gives the total resistance of the whole chain only. To find the voltage across one resistor, use V = IR with the current I of the whole chain.
model.ru: Правило R = R₁ + R₂ даёт только общее сопротивление всей цепи. Напряжение на одном резисторе находят по формуле U = IR, подставляя ток I всей цепи.

sources.title: Morris, Physics for the IB MYP 4 & 5: By Concept (Hodder, 2015)

parallelCircuit.name: Parallel circuit
parallelCircuit.definition: Components connected between the same two junctions, so each branch has the same potential difference.
parallelCircuit.example: Two 6 Ω resistors in parallel have equivalent resistance 3 Ω.

contrast.en: Branch currents can differ, but their sum is the current that enters the junction.
contrast.ru: Токи ветвей могут различаться, но их сумма равна току, входящему в узел.

model.en: The formula 1/R = 1/R₁ + 1/R₂ applies only to parallel resistors; series resistances simply add.
model.ru: Формула 1/R = 1/R₁ + 1/R₂ относится только к параллельным резисторам; последовательные сопротивления просто складываются.

sources.title: Morris, Physics for the IB MYP 4 & 5: By Concept (Hodder, 2015)

ohmicConductor.name: Ohmic conductor
ohmicConductor.definition: A conductor whose current is proportional to potential difference when temperature and other physical conditions are fixed.
ohmicConductor.example: A 5 Ω metal wire at constant temperature: 1 V gives 0.2 A, and 3 V gives 0.6 A.

contrast.en: Not every conductor is ohmic: a diode and a neon lamp do not obey Ohm's law.
contrast.ru: Не всякий проводник омический: диод и неоновая лампа закону Ома не подчиняются.

model.en: A metal's resistance rises as it heats up, so a test of Ohm's law must keep the temperature fixed.
model.ru: Сопротивление металла растёт при нагреве, поэтому при проверке закона Ома температуру держат постоянной.

sources.title: Morris, Physics for the IB MYP 4 & 5: By Concept (Hodder, 2015)

thermistor.name: Thermistor
thermistor.definition: A thermistor is a resistor whose resistance depends on temperature.
thermistor.example: If the temperature of a thermistor changes, its resistance changes, so at a fixed voltage the current in the circuit changes too.

contrast.en: A thermistor responds to temperature; an LDR responds to light.
contrast.ru: Термистор реагирует на температуру, фоторезистор — на освещённость.

model.en: Not every resistor that depends on temperature behaves the same way: in metals resistance rises when heated, in semiconductors it falls.
model.ru: Не все резисторы, зависящие от температуры, ведут себя одинаково: у металлов сопротивление при нагревании растёт, у полупроводников — падает.

ldr.name: LDR
ldr.definition: A light-dependent resistor whose resistance changes with illumination.
ldr.example: If the supply voltage stays the same, changing the light on an LDR changes its resistance and therefore the current (I = V/R).

contrast.en: An LDR senses illumination; it does not supply electrical energy like a solar cell.
contrast.ru: Фоторезистор чувствителен к освещению; он не служит источником энергии, как солнечный элемент.

model.en: How strongly an LDR responds depends on the wavelength of the light and on the material it is made from.
model.ru: Насколько сильно фоторезистор реагирует на свет, зависит от длины волны света и от материала, из которого он сделан.

staticElectricity.name: Static electricity
staticElectricity.definition: Static electricity is the effect of electric charge that stays on an object for some time.
staticElectricity.example: A large enough potential difference can drive a spark through the air.

contrast.en: Static electricity is not a steady current: a spark carries current only briefly.
contrast.ru: Статическое электричество — не постоянный ток: искра проводит ток лишь кратковременно.

model.en: Attraction alone does not prove opposite net charges: a charged body can attract a neutral one.
model.ru: Притяжение само по себе не доказывает противоположность зарядов: заряженное тело притягивает и нейтральное.

fuse.name: Fuse
fuse.definition: A protective component whose element melts when excessive current heats it enough, opening the circuit.
fuse.example: A fuse can interrupt a fault current that would overheat wiring.

contrast.en: After it operates, a fuse must be replaced, because its melted element cannot carry current again.
contrast.ru: Сработавший предохранитель нужно заменить: его плавкая вставка уже не может проводить ток.

model.en: It does not trip instantly at a precise current threshold; operation depends on current and duration.
model.ru: Срабатывание не мгновенно при строго заданном пороге: оно зависит от величины тока и длительности.

circuitBreaker.name: Circuit breaker
circuitBreaker.definition: A circuit breaker is a switch that opens the circuit by itself when there is an overload or a short circuit.
circuitBreaker.example: If too many high-power appliances are on one circuit, the current can become dangerously large, and the circuit breaker switches the circuit off.

contrast.en: Unlike a fuse, a circuit breaker does not melt.
contrast.ru: В отличие от предохранителя, автоматический выключатель не плавится.

model.en: A circuit breaker acts only when the current becomes dangerously large, so a normal current does not trip it.
model.ru: Автоматический выключатель срабатывает только тогда, когда ток становится опасно большим, поэтому обычный ток его не отключает.

efficiency.name: Efficiency
efficiency.definition: Useful output energy divided by total input energy, or useful output power divided by input power.
efficiency.example: 20 J of useful output from 100 J input gives efficiency 0.20, or 20%.

contrast.en: Efficiency is a ratio; power is an energy-transfer rate.
contrast.ru: КПД — отношение, а мощность — скорость передачи энергии.

kwh.name: Kilowatt-hour (kWh)
kwh.definition: The kilowatt-hour (kWh) is a unit of energy. It equals the energy transferred by 1 kW of power acting for 1 hour.
kwh.example: Electricity providers charge for energy in kWh. A 2 kW heater running for 0.5 h transfers 1 kWh.

contrast.en: kW is power; kWh is energy, not “kilowatts per hour”.
contrast.ru: кВт — мощность, кВт·ч — энергия, а не «киловатты в час».

model.en: A kWh value does not show how powerful a device is. A 3 kW kettle used for 0.1 h uses 0.3 kWh. A 0.1 kW lamp left on for 24 h uses 2.4 kWh.
model.ru: Значение в кВт·ч не показывает, насколько мощный прибор. Чайник мощностью 3 кВт, работающий 0,1 ч, расходует 0,3 кВт·ч. Лампа мощностью 0,1 кВт, горящая 24 ч, расходует 2,4 кВт·ч.

wavesOptics.title: Waves and Optics
wavesOptics.intro: From ripples on a pond to gamma rays — all waves share a few simple properties.

waveTypes.name: Transverse vs Longitudinal waves
waveTypes.rule: Transverse oscillations are perpendicular to propagation; longitudinal oscillations are parallel. Waves transfer energy and information. In the small-amplitude mechanical model, particles oscillate locally rather than travelling along with the wave.
examples: A stretched string can support transverse waves; air sound is longitudinal.
Electromagnetic waves have oscillating fields and do not require a material medium.

contrast.en: For electromagnetic waves it is the fields that oscillate, not material particles.
contrast.ru: В электромагнитной волне колеблются поля, а не частицы вещества.

model.en: Surface-water waves generally combine vertical and horizontal motion, so they are not purely transverse.
model.ru: Поверхностные волны на воде обычно сочетают вертикальное и горизонтальное движение и не являются чисто поперечными.

waveEquation.name: Wave equation: v = f·λ
waveEquation.rule: For a periodic travelling wave, v = fλ and T = 1/f. Frequency f counts cycles per second, wavelength λ measures spatial repetition and period T measures the time per cycle.
examples: At f = 50 Hz and λ = 2 m, v = 100 m/s and T = 0.02 s.
At a stationary boundary the transmitted wave keeps the source frequency; a speed change produces a wavelength change.

contrast.en: Frequency counts cycles per time; wave speed describes how fast a disturbance travels.
contrast.ru: Частота — число циклов за время; скорость волны — скорость распространения возмущения.

model.en: A single f and λ describe a periodic wave; a pulse can contain many frequencies.
model.ru: Одна пара f и λ описывает периодическую волну; импульс может содержать много частот.

emSpectrum.name: Electromagnetic spectrum
emSpectrum.rule: The electromagnetic spectrum is ordered by frequency or wavelength: radio → microwave → infrared → visible → ultraviolet → X-ray → gamma for increasing frequency. In vacuum all travel at c; photon energy E = hf increases with frequency.
examples: Radio waves carry communication signals; infrared radiation is used in thermal imaging.
X-rays and gamma rays can ionise matter. High-energy ultraviolet can also ionise; UV damage does not require every UV photon to be ionising.

contrast.en: Higher frequency means greater energy per photon, E = hf, not necessarily greater beam power.
contrast.ru: Большая частота означает большую энергию одного фотона E = hf, но не обязательно большую мощность пучка.

model.en: All travel at c in vacuum. Band boundaries are approximate, and radiation risk also depends on dose and exposure.
model.ru: В вакууме все распространяются со скоростью c. Границы диапазонов условны; риск зависит также от дозы и условий воздействия.

reflection.name: Reflection
reflection.rule: For a reflected ray, the angle of reflection equals the angle of incidence. Both angles are measured from the normal to the surface. A rough surface has different local normals and gives diffuse reflection.
examples: A ray incident at 40° to the normal reflects at 40° to the normal.
A plane mirror produces a virtual image as far behind the mirror as the object is in front.

contrast.en: Reflection returns into the original medium; refraction concerns the transmitted wave.
contrast.ru: Отражённая волна остаётся в исходной среде; преломлённая проходит в другую.

model.en: The ray law applies locally to a surface; rough surfaces scatter reflected rays in different directions.
model.ru: Закон для лучей действует локально: на шероховатой поверхности отражённые лучи идут в разных направлениях.

refraction.name: Refraction
refraction.rule: Refraction changes wave speed between media; at oblique incidence it usually changes direction. For light n = c/v and n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂, with angles measured from the normal. Larger n means lower light speed, not necessarily larger mass density.
examples: Air to glass at oblique incidence: the ray bends towards the normal.
Total internal reflection needs travel towards lower n and an incidence angle above the critical angle.

contrast.en: Use refractive index, not mass density, to predict the bending of light.
contrast.ru: Направление преломления света определяет показатель преломления, а не массовая плотность.

model.en: At normal incidence speed and wavelength change without bending; frequency stays the same at a stationary boundary.
model.ru: При падении по нормали скорость и длина волны меняются без поворота; на неподвижной границе частота сохраняется.

sound.name: Sound waves & hearing
sound.rule: Sound is a mechanical disturbance; in gases and liquids it propagates as longitudinal pressure waves. Pitch relates mainly to frequency; loudness depends on intensity, frequency and hearing. Sound speed depends on the medium’s elasticity and density.
examples: At room temperature sound speed in air is about 343 m/s, so a 3 s delay corresponds to about 1 km.
At fixed frequency and medium, increasing pressure amplitude increases intensity; amplitude itself is not measured in decibels.

contrast.en: Particles oscillate locally while the disturbance travels onward.
contrast.ru: Частицы колеблются около положения равновесия, а возмущение распространяется дальше.

model.en: The simple model describes small oscillations in a medium, without bulk transport by the wave.
model.ru: Простая модель описывает малые колебания среды без переноса её вещества вместе с волной.

amplitude.name: Amplitude
amplitude.definition: The maximum magnitude of an oscillating quantity’s deviation from its equilibrium value.
amplitude.example: For a string moving between −2 cm and +2 cm, displacement amplitude is 2 cm.

contrast.en: Amplitude is half the peak-to-peak range; wavelength is a distance along the wave.
contrast.ru: Амплитуда равна половине размаха; длина волны измеряется вдоль распространения.

model.en: For sound use displacement or pressure amplitude; for light use electric or magnetic field amplitude.
model.ru: Для звука рассматривают амплитуду смещения или давления; для света — амплитуду электрического или магнитного поля.

wavelength.name: Wavelength
wavelength.definition: The distance along a periodic wave between adjacent points in the same phase, measured at one time.
wavelength.example: From one crest to the next, or one compression to the next.

contrast.en: A wavelength is a spatial repeat; a period is the time for one cycle.
contrast.ru: Длина волны — пространственное повторение, период — время одного цикла.

model.en: Use adjacent matching points; the distance across two wavelengths is 2λ.
model.ru: Выбирай ближайшие однофазные точки: через две длины волны расстояние равно 2λ.

frequency.name: Frequency
frequency.definition: The number of complete oscillation cycles per unit time; 1 Hz means one cycle per second.
frequency.example: A source making 50 cycles each second has frequency 50 Hz and period 0.02 s.

contrast.en: Frequency counts cycles per time; wave speed describes how fast a disturbance travels.
contrast.ru: Частота — число циклов за время; скорость волны — скорость распространения возмущения.

model.en: A single f and λ describe a periodic wave; a pulse can contain many frequencies.
model.ru: Одна пара f и λ описывает периодическую волну; импульс может содержать много частот.

longitudinal.name: Longitudinal wave
longitudinal.definition: A wave whose oscillations are parallel to its direction of propagation.
longitudinal.example: In air, sound produces alternating compressions and rarefactions.

contrast.en: Particles oscillate locally while the disturbance travels onward.
contrast.ru: Частицы колеблются около положения равновесия, а возмущение распространяется дальше.

model.en: The simple model describes small oscillations in a medium, without bulk transport by the wave.
model.ru: Простая модель описывает малые колебания среды без переноса её вещества вместе с волной.

transverse.name: Transverse wave
transverse.definition: A wave whose oscillations are perpendicular to its direction of propagation.
transverse.example: A wave travels horizontally along a string while the string moves up and down.

contrast.en: For electromagnetic waves it is the fields that oscillate, not material particles.
contrast.ru: В электромагнитной волне колеблются поля, а не частицы вещества.

model.en: Surface-water waves generally combine vertical and horizontal motion, so they are not purely transverse.
model.ru: Поверхностные волны на воде обычно сочетают вертикальное и горизонтальное движение и не являются чисто поперечными.

emSpectrum.name: Electromagnetic spectrum
emSpectrum.definition: The continuous range of electromagnetic radiation, classified by frequency or wavelength.
emSpectrum.example: Increasing frequency: radio, microwave, infrared, visible, ultraviolet, X-ray, gamma.

contrast.en: Higher frequency means greater energy per photon, E = hf, not necessarily greater beam power.
contrast.ru: Большая частота означает большую энергию одного фотона E = hf, но не обязательно большую мощность пучка.

model.en: All travel at c in vacuum. Band boundaries are approximate, and radiation risk also depends on dose and exposure.
model.ru: В вакууме все распространяются со скоростью c. Границы диапазонов условны; риск зависит также от дозы и условий воздействия.

reflection.name: Reflection
reflection.definition: Return of a wave into the original medium after interaction with a boundary.
reflection.example: For a plane mirror, a ray at 30° to the normal reflects at 30°.

contrast.en: Reflection returns into the original medium; refraction concerns the transmitted wave.
contrast.ru: Отражённая волна остаётся в исходной среде; преломлённая проходит в другую.

model.en: The ray law applies locally to a surface; rough surfaces scatter reflected rays in different directions.
model.ru: Закон для лучей действует локально: на шероховатой поверхности отражённые лучи идут в разных направлениях.

refraction.name: Refraction
refraction.definition: A change in a wave’s speed on entering a different medium, usually accompanied by a change of direction.
refraction.example: An oblique ray entering glass from air bends towards the normal as it slows.

contrast.en: Use refractive index, not mass density, to predict the bending of light.
contrast.ru: Направление преломления света определяет показатель преломления, а не массовая плотность.

model.en: At normal incidence speed and wavelength change without bending; frequency stays the same at a stationary boundary.
model.ru: При падении по нормали скорость и длина волны меняются без поворота; на неподвижной границе частота сохраняется.

diffraction.name: Diffraction
diffraction.definition: Spreading and redistribution of a wave around an obstacle or after passage through an opening.
diffraction.example: Sound spreads through a doorway into regions outside a straight-line path.

contrast.en: Refraction requires a change of wave speed; diffraction can occur in one medium.
contrast.ru: Преломление связано с изменением скорости; дифракция возможна в одной среде.

model.en: Spreading is strongest when opening size is comparable to wavelength; diffraction is not absent for wider openings.
model.ru: Расхождение особенно заметно при размере отверстия порядка длины волны; при больших отверстиях дифракция не исчезает полностью.

lens.name: Lens
lens.definition: An optical element that refracts light to form an image or change a beam’s convergence.
lens.example: A converging lens can form a real image of a distant object on a screen.

contrast.en: A real image forms where rays meet; a virtual image forms where their backward extensions meet.
contrast.ru: Действительное изображение возникает в месте встречи лучей, мнимое — в месте встречи их обратных продолжений.

model.en: The thin-lens formula assumes a thin ideal lens and rays close to the principal axis.
model.ru: Формула тонкой линзы предполагает тонкую идеальную линзу и лучи вблизи главной оптической оси.

filter.name: Filter
filter.definition: An optical material that transmits some wavelength ranges more strongly than others.
filter.example: An ideal red filter under white light transmits red light and absorbs much of the rest.

contrast.en: A filter selects light already present; it does not turn every incoming colour into its own colour.
contrast.ru: Фильтр выделяет имеющийся свет, а не превращает любой входящий цвет в свой.

model.en: The simulation uses ideal colour bands; real filters have gradual, incomplete transmission and may also reflect light.
model.ru: Модель использует идеальные цветовые диапазоны; у реальных фильтров пропускание неполное и плавно меняется, возможны отражения.

criteria.title: MYP Criteria
criteria.intro: Four criteria are assessed in MYP Physics. Use the checklists to make sure your response covers everything.

A.title: Criterion A — Knowing & Understanding
A.subtitle: Recall and apply scientific knowledge (the written exam)
items: Recall scientific facts, terms and definitions accurately — vocabulary like 'momentum', 'resultant force', 'refraction' must be used precisely.
Apply scientific knowledge to solve problems in familiar situations (e.g. calculate F = ma when force and mass are given).
Apply scientific knowledge to solve problems in unfamiliar situations (transfer the same idea to a new context, e.g. why an airbag works).
Analyse and evaluate scientific information to make scientifically supported judgements.
Show your working in calculations: formula → substitution → answer → units.
Use the correct command term (state, describe, explain, compare, evaluate, calculate) when answering.

B.title: Criterion B — Inquiring & Designing
B.subtitle: Planning a lab
items: Clear research question with independent, dependent and controlled variables.
Hypothesis with scientific reasoning ('If… then… because…').
Materials and apparatus list with sizes / quantities.
Numbered method that another student could repeat exactly.
Safety considerations identified.
Plan for collecting enough data (≥ 5 values, ≥ 3 repeats).

C.title: Criterion C — Processing & Evaluating
C.subtitle: Analyzing a lab
items: Data table with units in headers and consistent decimal places.
Averages, ranges and uncertainties calculated.
Graph: title, labelled axes, suitable scale, line of best fit.
Trend described in words and linked to the science.
Conclusion answers the research question with evidence.
Evaluation: strengths, weaknesses and realistic improvements.

D.title: Criterion D — Reflecting on the Impacts of Science
D.subtitle: The essay
items: Clear scientific explanation of the issue.
Discussion of social, economic and environmental impacts.
Multiple perspectives considered (for / against / neutral).
Evidence from at least two reliable sources.
Personal opinion with justification.
References listed in a consistent format.
